name: Malveira da Serra, 6 October 2018

place: Serra de Sintra and Malveira da Serra (Sintra-Cascais Natural Park, near Lisbon, Portugal)
ignitionNote: Dramatisation. The real cause was never confirmed; the police investigated arson. A cigarette thrown from a car on a serra road is one way a fire like this can start. The game picks one of the ignitionCandidates each night (from the seed); the first one, beside the EN247 Rua do Cabo on the Peninha side, is also the fixed ignition.

wind.note: Open-Meteo ERA5 archive, 38.77 N, -9.46 W (Peninha ridge), 6 Oct 2018 22:00 local time. direction = where the wind comes FROM (degrees), speed and gust in km/h. A north wind pushes the fire south, down the mountain.

briefing: Serra de Sintra, near Lisbon. Saturday 6 October 2018, 22:50. After a dry summer, a strong north wind (33 km/h, gusts near 70 km/h) is blowing down the mountain towards Malveira da Serra and the small villages near Guincho beach. That night a real fire started in the scrub near the Peninha sanctuary. It crossed the EN247 road and ran downhill. Hundreds of people, a campsite and 70 horses were evacuated, 21 people were lightly hurt, and about 500 hectares burned before it was controlled at 10:45 the next morning. No aircraft could fly until dawn. The cause was never confirmed (the police investigated arson). You have 20,000 euros to prepare the town before the fire arrives.
aftermath: In real life: about 500 hectares burned in one night. Hundreds of people, a campsite and 70 horses were evacuated, and 21 people were lightly hurt. Around 700 firefighters fought the fire, but no aircraft could fly until dawn; it was controlled at 10:45 the next morning. Since then, the park has been cutting invasive trees and replanting native forest to make the next fire weaker.
ignitionHint: Tonight a cigarette thrown from a car will start a fire at one of the spots marked ? beside the serra roads. You will not know which one until it happens.

story: The map is the real ground around Malveira da Serra, 2.1 km on each side (one tile = 65 m, north at the top): heights from satellite elevation data, roads, houses and vegetation from OpenStreetMap. North is the steep south face of the Serra de Sintra: open scrub and granite on the west, towards the Peninha sanctuary just beyond the north-west corner, and dense pine and eucalyptus forest on the east, where a round hill with a bare rocky top rises over Janes. Malveira is not on a flat plain: it sits on a spur at the foot of the serra, where three or four valleys meet, and its white houses climb the slopes in tiers (about 140-180 m; the crest reaches about 365 m and the valleys in the south-west drop to about 80 m). The EN247 Rua do Cabo comes down from the west (the road to Azoia, Cabo da Roca and the Peninha turn-off) to the five-way junction at the largo by the chapel of Nossa Senhora da Assuncao. From there the EN247 goes south-west to Guincho, the EN9-1 Rua de Cascais goes south, the EN247-5 runs east to Janes, and the EN9-1 Estrada da Serra climbs north-east towards Sintra, with the Rua dos Capuchos and a road up the Portela valley branching off into the forest. A car drives along one of the serra roads and the fire starts in the dry scrub beside it (each night it can be a different spot). The fire station is a game stand-in: Malveira has no fire station (the nearest, the Bombeiros Voluntarios de Alcabideche, is 4 km away), so it stands where the real primary school is, on the EN9-1 at the top of the village. South are Alcorvim and Alto do Barril, villas among pine woods and scrub. The sea, Guincho beach and the hamlets of Biscaia and Figueira do Guincho are 2-3 km to the west and south-west, beyond the map; the land falls towards them.

mapSource.heights: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 via the Open-Meteo Elevation API, smoothed 3x3, then 0-9 linear from 85 m to 364 m (about 31 m per step).
mapSource.map: OpenStreetMap land cover (wood -> E, scrub/heath -> B, grass/farmland/garden -> G, bare rock -> C), buildings (3+ per tile -> H, sparse plots -> gardens G/O) and the main roads, drawn as one line each. The fire station tile and the dry verges at the cigarette spots are game choices.
